title: Fresh Fettuccine with Raw Tomato and Herb Sauce
changes_from_base: Shop-bought fresh fettuccine served under an uncooked sauce of ripe tomatoes, garlic, basil, oregano and parsley, with Parmesan.
summary: Hot fresh fettuccine under a cold, uncooked sauce of ripe tomatoes, garlic, herbs and Parmesan, made for high summer.

ingredients.item: very ripe tomatoes, cored and cut into chunks
Parmesan-style hard cheese (microbial rennet), finely grated
fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.5%)
ingredients.note: about 3.25 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

steps.title: Herbs
steps.text: With the processor running, drop the garlic through the feed tube to mince it. Stop, add the basil, oregano, parsley and oil and pulse to chop.

steps.title: Tomatoes
steps.text: Add the tomato chunks and pulse just until coarsely chopped; over-blending makes the sauce watery and pink.

steps.title: Cheese
steps.text: Tip into a bowl and stir in the Parmesan and pepper. The cheese seasons the sauce, so there is no added salt.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Boil the fettuccine in 4 litres salted water for 2-3 min until tender, then drain.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the hot pasta between bowls and spoon the cold sauce over at once. It only works with tomatoes at their summer best.

tips: Only make this with peak-season tomatoes.
Pulse the tomatoes briefly; a coarse sauce is better.
Warm the bowls so the pasta stays hot.
storage: Best eaten straight away. The sauce keeps refrigerated for up to 1 day. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
